extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO; USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; legal ethics/compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and enforcement principles used by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline to evaluate practitioner conduct (client communication, conflicts, acceptance/declination of referrals) and to impose sanctions/reinstatement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a),(b) via § 10.23(c)(8) — Duty to notify clients of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to inform clients of correspondence received from the Office when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) is received by the practitioner on behalf of a client or former client, and (iii) is correspondence of which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client or former client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements to satisfy the duty: the correspondence must be significant to the pending matter, received on behalf of the client, and of a kind that a reasonable practitioner would notify the client about. Failure to notify in such circumstances violates the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) — Acceptance of referred clients without informed consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Not refusing employment and instead accepting referred clients from a referring entity without the consent of the referred client after full disclosure, including not adequately describing escrow and payment arrangements for patent legal services where the practitioner's professional judgment may be affected by the practitioner's own financial, business, property, or personal interests (e.g., practitioner's business relationship with the referring entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must disclose relationships and payment/escrow arrangements and obtain client consent after full disclosure before accepting such referrals; failing to do so violates §10.62(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(a) — Declining employment when independent judgment likely adversely affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to decline employment from a referring entity where the exercise of the practitioner's independent professional judgment on behalf of a client will be or is likely to be adversely affected by acceptance of the proffered employment or if it would be likely to involve representing differing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a referral or business relationship with a referring entity creates a substantial risk that the practitioner's independent judgment will be compromised or will pose differing interests, the practitioner must decline the employment or otherwise avoid the conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — Duty to act on legal matters entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to act on legal matters entrusted to the practitioner, including failing to communicate with referred clients adequately and in a timely manner about their applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule encompasses affirmative obligations to take appropriate actions, to supervise staff adequately, to respond to Office actions, and to keep clients timely apprised of status and options; neglect or inaction in prosecution can violate §10.77(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate client communication and involvement during patent prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must (and here failed to) speak directly with clients about their inventions, the legal services to be performed, the patentability opinion, and the patent prosecution process; engage in pre-filing discussions; timely inform clients of Office actions; explain their significance; counsel clients on response options and consequences; assist clients in making decisions; refrain from taking action on applications without clients' knowledge; keep clients fully and timely apprised of application status (directly or via adequate staff supervision); and not allow applications to be abandoned without client consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative anti-patterns include not contacting clients about substantive matters, failing to explain Office actions or options, permitting abandonment without client approval, acting on applications without client involvement, and failing to supervise staff so that clients are left uninformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure and obtaining informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must disclose business relationships with referring entities (e.g., ISC), disclose actual or potential conflicts presented by escrow/payment arrangements or other financial/business ties, and obtain client consent after full disclosure before representing referred clients in light of that relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose the business relationship and potential conflicts, or to obtain informed consent after disclosure, constitutes professional misconduct under the cited rules (and was a central factual/legal finding in this matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions, conditions for suspension, and reinstatement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary remedies imposed and procedural conditions: suspension from practice before the USPTO for specified term (here, 36 months); limited recognition for a short period (30 days) to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b); requirements to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; prohibition on applying for or obtaining a Customer Number until reinstated; ability to petition for reinstatement after six months (pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60); probationary period (24 months) if reinstated; Order to Show Cause procedures and possible additional suspension during probation for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps: OED issues Order to Show Cause, sends to respondent's last address, grants 15 days to respond; if OED remains of the opinion there's a violation it delivers materials to the USPTO Director and may request additional suspension up to 30 months. Reinstatement is subject to OED Director's grant and probation conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements for disciplinary actions (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a notice materially consistent in the Official Gazette; pursuant to § 11.59, give notice of public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes an Official Gazette notice summarizing the violations and sanctions; dissemination of information if suspended during probation (dissociation of Customer Numbers and PKI certificates, notification to agencies). The order cites a URL for the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors to be considered in determining discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors considered mitigating in this settlement: no prior disciplinary history before the Office during over twenty years of registration; respondent experienced a serious medical condition that impaired ability to practice and adversely affected judgment during part of the relevant period; respondent fully cooperated with OED during investigation and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating factors were specifically cited as influencing the settlement and sanction imposed; they may reduce severity of discipline in similar cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) in future complaints or proceedings concerning the respondent, either as an aggravating factor in determining future discipline or to rebut statements by or on behalf of the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's disciplinary history may be invoked later to escalate sanctions or to counter mitigation claims; the record remains available for future disciplinary consideration.
